To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(a) the user interface is a crucial part of any software engineering environment, (b) the user interface should be uniform and consistent, (c) it should be customisable, and (d) it should include a set of “minor” functionalities.

the development of a good user interface requires: (1) a careful analysis of the environment to be developed and the user’s needs and habits, (2) the application of the principles of uniformity, customizability, and consistency, and (3) a proper mixture of minor facilities.

the development of a good user interface for a software engineering environment requires the following: (i) a proper mixture of uniformity, customizability, and consistency; (ii) a proper mixture between major and minor facilities, such as command completion, history editing, and online help; (iii) the use of a proper graphical user interface; and (iv) the use of proper programming techniques for the implementation of a user interface.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a software engineering tool that is easy to use and learn.
the definition of a paradigm for the design and construction of a user interface that supports the development of software engineering environments.
the design and implementation of the User- Tool Interaction Subsystem in the GRASPIN programming environment.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
a good interface should be designed and developed in a way that the user feels comfortable and at home, as if he were using a well-known and familiar environment.
the User-Tool Interface Subsystem of GRASPIN is a well-designed and well-engineered component that provides a good user interface for a variety of tools.
a user interface that does not provide the user with a consistent, customizable, and uniform environment, together with minor facilities, is doomed to failure.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
a user interface is a crucial component for the success of an environment, and its design and implementation should be given a lot of attention and care.
the user should be able to concentrate his/her effort on the task at hand rather than on the interface.
the User-Tool Interface Subsystem of GRASPIN has been designed to be an integral part of the environment, rather than a separate component.
The main takeaway from our work is that
, in addition to the technical issues, the development of the User- Tool Interaction Subsystem is also a social process.
a user interface can be built in a modular fashion, and that it can be easily tailored to the needs of a specific environment.
a good user interface can be built on top of a simple and uniform architecture.
